summary: vanexa-agent bundles a WebSocket-driven remote shell routed through an author-controlled Cloudflare Worker
details: dist/bundle.cjs (loaded as V8 bytecode dist/bundle.jsc via a postinstall bytenode compile step) opens a WebSocket connection to vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev, an author-controlled Cloudflare Worker, and spawns a persistent local shell/PTY (VANEXA_PERSISTENT_SHELL / VANEXA_PTY_DONE_) via child_process.spawn. Messages received on the WebSocket drive further spawn/exec calls on the host, giving whoever controls the relay endpoint a live shell on the installer's machine. The README frames the tool as LAN-only phone control, but the traced data path routes command flow through the author's cloud relay rather than a LAN peer. Alongside this, an AI-provider baseUrl of https://vanexa-ai-proxy.hanazaki542.workers.dev appears in the bundle and receives user prompts under specific apiKey conditions, contradicting the README's BYOK no-middleman claim. The shipped code is a 2.2 MB minified single-line bundle compiled to opaque V8 bytecode at postinstall, making the network-to-shell dataflow difficult to audit.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
